channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Marine
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Hackers reportedly reached a US-bound tanker’s propulsion system; no agency has confirmed it, and the FBI reports no disruption
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 2 October, citing unnamed US officials, that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found outsiders had briefly accessed digital systems aboard the supertanker VL Prosperity, including its propulsion system, as it approached Texas this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that finding on the record, and how long the access lasted or what the intruders could control is unclear. The FBI says there are no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental harm. In September the Coast Guard said it had found evidence of a malicious cyber actor aboard. The Liberian-flagged tanker was boarded on 21 August in the Atlantic, per Dragos, after losing communications; its manager, HMM Ocean Service, confirmed the boarding. A second, unnamed tanker was boarded on 24 August in the Gulf of Mexico. No attacker has been named, and no new official finding had appeared by 16 October. - Bloomberg, 2 Oct 2026, citing unnamed US officials (via gCaptain, 5 Oct); FBI statement; Coast Guard (Rear Adm. Grable, via CBS News); Dragos, 24 Sep (boarding locations); Baird Maritime, 7 Oct (manager’s confirmation of the boarding) - Boardings 21 & 24 Aug 2026; propulsion-access report 2 Oct; no agency confirmation of that finding as of 16 Oct

item.title: [Medium] Extortion group n0n claims data from 38 port, shipping and logistics firms; none has confirmed a breach
item.category: Incident (claimed) — Extortion group lists port, shipping and logistics firms; unverified
item.description: On 12 October the data-theft extortion group n0n, first seen in September 2026, posted 38 maritime and logistics organizations in 18 countries to its leak site in one batch, SOCRadar reported the next day; 12 of the listings are in South Korea. They cover container-terminal operators, shipping lines, port IT providers and logistics firms; listed names include Pusan Newport Co., Santos Brasil, TTI Algeciras, Eurogate Tanger, a Singapore office of Ocean Network Express and crane maker ZPMC. The group says it holds EDI messages, manifests, vessel schedules, gate movements and terminal configuration records, and demands $2.4–14 million in bitcoin before a 19 October publication deadline. SOCRadar calls every claim unverified. n0n usually enters with infostealer-harvested credentials, but SOCRadar found no such matches for many listed firms and suspects one shared, exposed application instead; Cydome, quoted by Maritime Executive, pointed to a possible compromise of an environment shared through a maritime software provider, with source and scope unconfirmed. No listed organization has confirmed or denied a breach, and no operational disruption is reported. - SOCRadar, 13 Oct 2026 (analysis of the leak-site listings); The Loadstar and Maritime Executive (Cydome comment), 14 Oct 2026; Industrial Cyber, 15 Oct 2026 - Batch posted 12 Oct 2026; publication deadline 19 Oct 2026, 13:27 UTC — claims unverified

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service say the FortiBleed credential-theft campaign against Fortinet gateways is still active
item.category: Campaign — Credential theft against Fortinet firewalls and SSL VPNs, no CVE
item.description: In a joint advisory dated 6 October, the FBI and US Secret Service warned that attackers are still scanning internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways with credentials gathered earlier in the campaign. No vulnerability is involved: the agencies point to reused or leaked passwords and legacy SHA-256 password storage, and researchers describe offline hash cracking and a tool that sniffs login traffic across 24 protocols. Intruders have created rogue admin accounts and deleted or reset legitimate ones, locking owners out, and the access is resold; SOCRadar says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments from it. The agencies say targeted organizations span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, a set that includes transportation systems. SOCRadar’s figure of 86,644 working device credentials across 194 countries dates from 19 June and is not a new count. No maritime or OT victim has been named. Editorial assessment: FortiGate appliances commonly guard links between shipping offices, terminals and remote sites. - FBI/US Secret Service joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01, 6 Oct 2026 (primary); Cybersecurity Dive and The Hacker News, 7 Oct 2026 - Advisory 6 Oct 2026; campaign first documented June 2026; credential count as of 19 Jun 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco Secure FMC, a common firewall console at IT/OT boundaries, remains under active exploitation
item.category: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco Talos tracks three clusters exploiting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center flaws. UAT-12197 used CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0), an authentication bypass, to deploy web shells. UAT-11823 used both flaws and deployed a Cyclops Blink implant; Talos notes tooling overlaps for this cluster but makes no attribution. UAT-11988, a ransomware operator, used CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3), which Talos says can be chained for privilege escalation, then set up proxy and SSH tunnels before deploying ransomware. Talos names no victims, sectors or countries, and its post was last updated 21 September. Editorial assessment: FMC often manages the firewalls between corporate IT and terminal-operating-system, crane and gate networks at ports. - Cisco Talos analysis, published 9 Sep 2026, last updated 21 Sep 2026 (primary); The Hacker News, 11 Sep 2026 - Exploitation confirmed early Sep 2026; latest Talos update 21 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Google ties a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, exploited since late August, to a suspected China-nexus espionage group
item.category: Threat Intelligence — Exploited remote-support zero-day, suspected state-nexus actor
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group said on 15 October that the suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it tracks as ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4.0 9.3) in BeyondTrust Remote Support as a zero-day from late August. SecurityWeek reports two appliances were compromised, one hosted by BeyondTrust and one self-hosted. The intruders gained root, harvested credentials, deleted logs and used the product’s file-transfer feature to pull documents from users’ desktops. BeyondTrust identified the defect on 28 September, shipped a fix on 8 October and had patched its SaaS customers by 9 October; self-hosted customers without automatic updates must patch manually. GTIG names no victims or sectors and advises treating any internet-reachable appliance that ran a vulnerable version during the window as potentially compromised. Editorial assessment: OEMs and service providers use remote-support tools like this to reach vessel and terminal workstations. - Google Threat Intelligence Group, 15 Oct 2026 (primary); SecurityWeek, 16 Oct 2026 - Exploited from late Aug 2026; fix shipped 8 Oct; SaaS patched 9 Oct; disclosed 15 Oct

item.title: [Medium] ENISA: China-nexus intrusion sets showed continuous interest in transport, including maritime entities
item.category: Threat Intelligence — EU threat landscape, maritime espionage interest
item.description: The EU cybersecurity agency’s Threat Landscape 2026 report, covering calendar 2025 and published 22–23 September, says China-nexus intrusion sets showed continuous interest in the transport sector, including maritime entities, per Industrial Cyber’s summary. ENISA’s own summary puts transport at 8% of the events it analysed, level with business services and behind public administration at 32%, and its NIS360 assessment lists maritime among sectors that are highly critical but less mature. Ransomware remained the most damaging threat, and 60% of unauthorized-access incidents leveraged known vulnerabilities. The report describes long-running intelligence-collection interest rather than a specific new operation against ships or ports, and it does not name a vessel or terminal victim. - ENISA Threat Landscape 2026 and ENISA press release (22 Sep 2026); Industrial Cyber, 23 Sep 2026 - Covers 1 Jan–31 Dec 2025; published 22–23 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FDD report: Chinese-operated port terminals and patchy cyber oversight expose NATO’s European mobility corridors
item.category: Research — Port ownership and NATO military mobility
item.description: A Foundation for Defense of Democracies report by Jiwon Ma, published 28 September, argues that foreign ownership and fragmented cyber oversight weaken the ports, railways and roads NATO would use to move forces across Europe. It says Chinese state-linked firms hold stakes in more than 30 European port terminals and, citing a 2023 European Parliament study, that COSCO Shipping, China Merchants and Hutchison Port Holdings own or operate terminals in roughly half of the EU ports considered critical to NATO. It also finds that civilian transport operators lack consistent security standards across NATO, EU and national authorities, and recommends tighter EU investment screening plus authentication and alternative navigation procedures against satellite interference. The “state-linked” characterization is FDD’s; the report describes structural exposure, not an intrusion at any port. - FDD report, 28 Sep 2026 (primary; registration required to download); Industrial Cyber, 30 Sep 2026 - Published 28 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] Honeywell survey: 87% of maritime respondents reported a significant OT incident in the past year
item.description: Honeywell’s 2026 OT Cybersecurity Benchmark, published 22 September and based on more than 600 industrial security leaders worldwide, found that 87% of maritime respondents reported a significant OT cybersecurity incident in the past 12 months, and 40% of maritime respondents named outdated equipment as their main obstacle. Across all sectors only 21% kept a complete OT asset inventory and average downtime from major incidents was 16.2 hours. This is a vendor survey of self-reported incidents; definitions of “significant” vary and it identifies no specific vessel or port. - Honeywell press release, 22 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber - Published 22 Sep 2026; survey of 600+ respondents

item.title: [Critical] Ivanti Connect Secure: a three-flaw chain gave attackers root on fully patched VPNs, and one link is still unpatched
item.category: Advisory — Exploited VPN zero-day chain, CISA KEV, one flaw unpatched
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a chain of three flaws gave unauthenticated attackers root on fully patched Connect Secure appliances at a limited number of customers. Two of the flaws are fixed under one CVE, CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS v3.1 8.6), which CISA added to KEV the same day with a 16 October deadline; the third, a privilege-escalation bug, has no CVE and no patch yet. Volexity found the chain during an incident response and tracks a new actor, UTA0576; exploitation dates from at least early October, with Volexity and Defused placing it at 1–3 October. The intruders left no web shell, stole domain credentials, queried Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, sprayed passwords and wiped logs. Volexity and CISA warn that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker may not detect the compromise. Editorial assessment: Connect Secure is a common remote-access gateway for shipping offices, terminal operators and their vendors. - Ivanti advisory and Volexity research, 13 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA KEV, 13 Oct 2026; CyberScoop and Cybersecurity Dive (Defused), 13–14 Oct 2026 - Exploited from 1–3 Oct 2026; disclosed and added to KEV 13 Oct; federal deadline 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler: a fourth critical flaw follows three exploited zero-days, and recently patched SAML appliances need another upgrade
item.category: Advisory — Fourth critical flaw after three exploited zero-days, CISA KEV
item.description: Citrix disclosed a fourth critical NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaw on 8 October in bulletin CTX697191: CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5), a memory overflow on appliances configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider that Citrix says may lead to remote code execution or denial of service. No exploitation of it has been reported and it is not in KEV, but builds that fixed the September zero-days (14.1-73.37 to 73.41 and 13.1-64.23 to 64.28) stay vulnerable when used as a SAML IdP, so those appliances need another upgrade. Three earlier flaws are exploited and in KEV: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (both CVSS 9.5, added 27 September) and CVE-2026-88779 (added 4 October), which Citrix and watchTowr describe as a denial-of-service bug. Cybersecurity Dive reported on 12 October that CISA again urged patching, warning that attackers use 88779 to force reboots so code planted through 88771 runs. Mandiant links the activity only to suspected state-nexus actors and counts dozens of affected organizations; Arctic Wolf tracks at least 78 targeted organizations, and Shadowserver sees more than 20,000 exposed or potentially vulnerable appliances. Editorial assessment: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door into port, terminal and OT DMZ networks. - Citrix bulletins CTX697174 (3 Oct) and CTX697191 (8 Oct); CISA KEV; CVE-2026-107406 record (NetScaler CNA); Cybersecurity Dive, 12 Oct 2026 (CISA warning, Shadowserver, Mandiant, Arctic Wolf); The Hacker News, 9 Oct; watchTowr via SecurityWeek, 5 Oct - Zero-days patched 27 Sep and 3 Oct 2026; fourth flaw disclosed 8 Oct; CISA renewed its warning by 12 Oct

item.title: [High] SonicWall SMA1000: honeypots logged attempts against a CVSS 10 pre-authentication flaw two days after the fix
item.category: Advisory — Maximum-severity remote-access flaw, exploitation attempts reported
item.description: SonicWall fixed CVE-2026-102255 on 6 October (advisory SNWLID-2026-0017): a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 WorkPlace interface that lets an unauthenticated attacker make the appliance send requests to its own internal functions. CISA’s enrichment scores it CVSS v3.1 10.0, and SonicWall calls it maximum severity. Defused saw the first hits on its decoys on 8 October and Previdian counted 135 attempts from two US addresses, SecurityWeek reported on 12 October; neither has shown that any attempt succeeded, and the flaw is not in KEV. Affected are SMA 6210, 7210 and 8200v appliances on 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 and earlier; SMA 100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected. Three authenticated flaws were fixed alongside it, and SMA1000 has been repeatedly exploited in 2026. Editorial assessment: these appliances often give integrators and OEMs a path toward port and fleet-support networks. - SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0017, 6 Oct 2026 (primary); CVE record with CISA-ADP scoring; SecurityWeek, 12 Oct 2026 (Defused, Previdian) - Fixed 6 Oct 2026; attempts first seen 8 Oct; reported 12 Oct

item.title: [High] Toptech TMS7 and TopHAT: ten flaws up to CVSS 10.0 in terminal-management software, fixed in release 7.8
item.category: Advisory — Terminal-management software, CVSS 10.0, fix available
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-02 (29 September) covers ten vulnerabilities in Toptech Systems TMS7 and TopHAT 7.6.3. The most severe, CVE-2026-71379 (CVSS 10.0), leaves files and directories accessible to external parties; CVE-2026-70356 (9.1) allows unrestricted file upload, and five SQL-injection flaws score 9.0. CISA says exploitation could let an attacker access critical data or execute arbitrary code, and lists the Energy, Chemical and Transportation Systems sectors, with deployments worldwide. Toptech notified customers on 20 July and fixed all the issues in release 7.8. CISA reports no known public exploitation. Editorial assessment: Toptech’s terminal-management software is used at fuel and bulk-liquid terminals, including those in ports, so marine terminal operators should check whether they run it. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-02, 29 Sep 2026 (primary; CSAF via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup) - Advisory 29 Sep 2026; vendor notice to customers 20 Jul 2026; fixed in 7.8

item.title: [High] Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard hard-coded keys: CISA advisory names two CVEs and the fixed build
item.category: Advisory — Hard-coded cryptographic keys, fix available, no known exploitation
item.description: CISA’s advisory ICSA-26-258-02 (15 September) covers two hard-coded cryptographic key flaws (CWE-321) in Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard 5.07.0923.01, a shipboard fleet-optimization system: CVE-2026-81855 in its robot testing framework and CVE-2026-78225 in its deployer-ng Update Controller. Published CVSS scores for the pair conflict between records, from 9.0–9.1 with a network attack vector to 8.3 with an adjacent-network vector, so check the current advisory before setting priority. Per CISA, an attacker could deliver an unauthorized update, execute code or extract credentials. The fix is 5.08.4052.01, obtained through Wärtsilä’s FOS download site or patch-deployment service; the CVE records were updated on 24 September to point there. Wärtsilä says the flaws are not exploitable when the product is installed as recommended, and Cydome, which reported them, credits the vendor with a patch. No exploitation has been reported. A hard-coded key is shared across installations, so one recovered key could work fleet-wide. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-258-02, 15 Sep 2026 (primary; CSAF via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup); CVE records (CNA: ICS-CERT), updated 24 Sep 2026; Hellenic Shipping News (Cydome finding) - Advisory published 15 Sep 2026; CVE references updated 24 Sep; fixed version 5.08.4052.01

item.title: [Medium] Lantronix G520 cellular gateways: a leaked signing key lets attackers push trusted firmware; update to 2.6.0.7R6
item.category: Advisory — Cellular gateway update-signing flaw, fix available
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-01 (29 September) covers two flaws in Lantronix G520 Series cellular gateways running 2.6.0.4R6_stable, each CVSS 7.5 (v3.1). CVE-2026-91191 is a signature-verification failure in the update mechanism: per the advisory, the publicly distributed SDK contains the production private key, so an attacker could sign malicious packages the gateway will trust. CVE-2026-84409 is a cross-site scripting flaw in how the web interface displays update metadata fetched over plain HTTP. CISA says exploitation could let an attacker replace software and run code with root privileges, and lists Transportation Systems, Energy and Water and Wastewater among affected sectors. Lantronix fixed both in firmware 2.6.0.7R6; no exploitation has been reported. Editorial assessment: cellular gateways like these often link remote port-side equipment and terminal sensors back to control centers. - CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-01, 29 Sep 2026 (primary; CSAF via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup) - Advisory 29 Sep 2026; fixed in 2.6.0.7R6

item.title: [High] CISA and the FBI name transportation among sectors exposed through a compromised ICS integrator
item.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrator remote access
item.description: A joint FBI/CISA fact sheet on working with third-party ICS integrators, published 24 September, describes foreign cyber actors who compromised a US industrial automation company in March–April 2025 and created nine .zip files of about 800 files, including SCADA-related data, for presumed exfiltration. It names power utilities and transportation among the affected customers. It urges least privilege for integrators, secured remote-access points, offline backups and cybersecurity terms in contracts. Editorial assessment: shipyards, OEMs and other service providers often hold standing remote access to vessel and terminal control systems, so the guidance applies directly to marine operators. - FBI/CISA fact sheet, published 24 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber, 24 Sep 2026 - Cites a March–April 2025 intrusion at a US automation integrator

item.title: [Info] NIST’s draft SP 800-82 Rev. 4 brings maritime vessels into its OT security guide; comments close 30 November
item.category: Guidance — Draft OT security guide now covers maritime vessels
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, its Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security, on 21 September. The revision expands coverage to maritime vessels, building automation, water and wastewater, and freight rail, and reorganizes the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, moving risk management under the Govern function and adding Risk Management Framework appendices. It also strengthens asset-management and network-monitoring guidance and adds zero-trust architecture material, reflecting IIoT and cloud connections into OT. Comments are due 30 November 2026. This is voluntary draft guidance; for US-regulated vessels and facilities, the Coast Guard’s MTSA cybersecurity rule sets the binding requirements. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft, 21 Sep 2026 (primary) - Released 21 Sep 2026; comment period closes 30 Nov 2026
